title: Cylindrical rod
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw the first two-dimensional sketch on the first face. In the first loop, draw four lines to form a square: the first line from the origin (0.0, 0.0) to (0.0201, 0.0), the second line from (0.0201, 0.0) to (0.0201, 0.0201), the third line from (0.0201, 0.0201) to (0.0, 0.0201), and the fourth line from (0.0, 0.0201) back to the origin. In the second loop, draw another smaller square inside the first one: the first line from (0.0004, 0.0004) to (0.0197, 0.0004), the second line from (0.0197, 0.0004) to (0.0197, 0.0197), the third line from (0.0197, 0.0197) to (0.0004, 0.0197), and the fourth line from (0.0004, 0.0197) back to (0.0004, 0.0004). Apply a scale factor of 0.0201 to the entire sketch to adjust its size. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three-dimensional space by rotating it using Euler angles set to zero degrees and translating it using a translation vector set to zero. Finally, extrude the sketch 0.75 units along the normal direction to generate the three-dimensional model. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction. The final dimensions of the cylindrical rod with a sharp pointed tip are a length of 0.020053475935828877 units, a width of 0.020053475935828877 units, and a height of 0.75 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(0.0201, 0).lineTo(0.0201, 0.0201).lineTo(0, 0.0201).close()

# Define the inner loop
inner_loop = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0.0004, 0.0004).lineTo(0.0197, 0.0004).lineTo(0.0197, 0.0197).lineTo(0.0004, 0.0197).close()

# Create the face by combining the outer and inner loops
face = sketch.add(inner_loop)

# Extrude the face to create the 3D object
extrusion = face.extrude(0.75)

# Create the final model
r = extrusion
